newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia prepared to talk on Russia air dispute.
newsitem.headline: Latvia prepared to talk on Russia air dispute.

text.p: Latvia wants talks on its dispute with Russia over flying rights between the two countries, Latvian Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said on Monday.
"We are prepared to talk on any of the issues involved, but they must be viewed in context," Krishtopans told Latvian radio.
Aeroflot last week suspended flights to Riga after Latvia refused to confirm its winter schedule in protest at a lack of flying rights for Latvia's Air Baltic to Russia.
Russia says Air Baltic, in which Scandinavian Airlines has a large stake, must repay debts run up by the former state carrier, Latavio.

But Latvia says it is owed money by Russia for using Riga airport when it withdrew its troops from the Baltic state in 1994, three years after Latvia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union.
Latvia says Russia owes it around one million dollars.
"Talks are the only reasonable way out if we do not want to unnecessarily politicise the issue," Arnis Muizhnieks, head of Latvia's transport ministry aviation department, told Reuters.
"This is a business question," he added.
Latvia says that under international conventions it should have two airlines operating to Russia to match the two, Aeroflot and Transaero, that operate to Riga.
Up to now, only Latvia's Riair, which has a code-sharing agreement with Transaero, has been allowed to fly to Moscow.
Scandinavian Airlines has a large stake in Air Baltic but the new airline had a worse than expected peformance in its first year of operation.
One of the reasons cited was the lack of flying rights to Moscow, a key market for the Baltics.
